claims.text: Refractory alloys can have extremely high melting points.
The target refractory alloy is initially a solid at temperatures well below its melting point.
A machine-learning interatomic potential trained on high-temperature DFT data can reproduce the melting properties of high-melting refractory alloys with near first-principles accuracy.
The machine-learning approach costs substantially less than full ab initio free-energy calculations.
Moment tensor potentials or neural-network potentials can be trained on curated high-temperature DFT data and deployed in large-scale molecular dynamics simulations.
Molecular dynamics with a machine-learning potential combined with thermodynamic integration can calculate melting temperature, fusion entropy, fusion enthalpy, and volume change at melting.
Simulations should span the expected melting point and sufficiently sample both solid and liquid phases.
The relevant mediator is the atomic configurations and interatomic-force landscape represented by the machine-learning potential.
Training on high-fidelity DFT data allows the machine-learning potential to reproduce free-energy differences between solid and liquid states accurately.
Accurate solid-liquid free-energy differences permit extraction of the melting temperature through thermodynamic integration.
Fusion entropy, fusion enthalpy, and volume change at melting can be derived using the proposed machine-learning thermodynamic-integration workflow.
The proposed workflow drastically reduces computational expense relative to DFT thermodynamic integration.
Machine-learning predictions will fall within an acceptable error margin of DFT free-energy calculations.
The computational savings will enable high-throughput screening of refractory alloys.
Incomplete coverage of high-temperature atomic environments in the DFT training set can limit the method's reliability.
Extrapolation to alloy compositions substantially outside the training domain can limit the method's reliability.
Prediction errors may vary with alloy composition and temperature range.
